tagline: A short loop down Boone's Creek to a fox hunt's mill.
intro: The loop starts on KY 418 near Athens and runs over the line into Clark County, comes back by Grimes Mill Road past the old stone mill on Boone's Creek, and returns to KY 418 by McCalls Mill Road. It is 8.6 miles around.

Daniel Boone built a fort in 1775 half a mile west of where Athens stands. The village was Cross Plains before it was Athens, and it once had a woolen factory and a bagging and rope works, until fires took them all by 1860.

moments.title: Athens
moments.text: A fire in 1853 and 1854 swept away the business houses on the south side of Main Street, but the log and frame Dr. Parker House and the brick Marshall Tavern still stand.

moments.title: Grimes Mill
moments.text: The quarried stone walls are three and a half feet thick, and since 1928 the old mill has housed a hunt named for the first American-bred horse to win the Epsom Derby.
